name: JS Swarm Points
description: JavaScript node demo: an orbital swarm of up to 128 points simulated in JS (attractors, swirl, separation, mouse, kick; dt-correct sub-steps) and sent to the GPU with dataTexture(); a GLSL node draws glowing metaballs and links between near points, with Feedback trails. Tweak it in the Parameters panel (P): Swarm, Look and Music.

data.text:
# JS Swarm Points
A JavaScript node simulates up to 128 points orbiting drifting attractors, finds the pairs that are close, and sends both lists to the GPU as data textures; a GLSL node draws them as glowing metaballs joined by light links.
Move the mouse over the preview: the swarm follows it (or flees, see the Mouse param) while it moves. Reacts to music: the kick bursts the orbits outward.
## What the JS does
- Setup (runs once): typed arrays in state for positions, velocities and hues, plus the two output buffers.
- Every frame: forces = spring toward the point's attractor + a perpendicular swirl (orbits) + separation + mouse + kick, integrated with semi-implicit Euler in fixed 1/120 s sub-steps (frame-rate independent).
- Then it lists links (pairs closer than Link distance, at most 192) and returns { points: dataTexture(pts, 128, 1, 4), links: dataTexture(links, 192, 2, 4), count, linkCount }.
- In GLSL, point i is texelFetch(points, ivec2(i, 0), 0) = (x, y, speed, hue); link i is texel (i, 0) = (x1, y1, x2, y2) and (i, 1) = (strength, hue1, hue2).
## Make it yours
Double-click the JS node (Swarm Sim group): change the forces (try gravity 1/d² instead of the spring, or flocking), give points other data in the free channels, or raise MAXL for more links. Swarm Field (Render group) is plain GLSL: change the look there.
## Tweak it in the Parameters panel
Press P: Swarm, Look and Music settings; hover a name for what it does, double-click a slider to reset it.
Double-click a group box to open it, Esc to come back.

## Swarm Sim (JS)
Reads params['Points'], ['Attractors'], ['Speed'], ['Swirl'], ['Link distance'], ['Mouse'], ['Kick burst'] by label, plus mouse, dt, time and audio.kick.
state keeps the simulation between frames; dt-correct sub-steps keep it stable at any frame rate.

## Render
Swarm Field loops over the points (metaball field sum r²/d², iso rim, white-hot cores where blobs merge, soft halos) and the links (distance to each segment, glow falloff), then keeps max(new, last frame × Trails) from an rgba16f Feedback. ACES, vignette and grain finish it.

data.label: Points
data.description: How many points are alive (up to 128).

data.label: Attractors
data.description: Number of drifting attractors the points orbit.

data.label: Swirl
data.description: Sideways push: 0 = points fall into the attractors, higher = wider, faster orbits.

data.label: Mouse
data.description: What the mouse does while it moves over the preview.

data.label: Link distance
data.description: Points closer than this are joined by a link (at most 192 links).

data.label: Glow
data.description: Brightness of blobs, halos and links.

data.label: Trails
data.description: How much of the last frame stays.

data.label: Colour A
data.description: One end of the point colour gradient.

data.label: Colour B
data.description: Other end of the point colour gradient.

data.label: Kick burst
data.description: How hard the kick drum bursts the orbits outward (audio menu: Metronome, Mic or a music file).
